# Adjudication Task — Chapter 247

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃247화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|음습한 지하 도박장. 구석 자리에 앉아 골패를 만지작거리고 있던 중년인이 고개를 떨궜다.
  6|
  7|“……죽겠소.”
  8|
  9|그의 코에는 서역에서 들어온 안경이라는 물건이 걸쳐져 있었는데, 며칠 전만 해도 은자 수십 냥은 족히 나갈 물건이었지만 지금은 아니었다.
 10|
 11|사물을 몇 배나 키워서 보여 준다는 안경알이 가뭄이 든 논처럼 쩍쩍 금이 가 있었기 때문이다.
 12|
 13|먼발치에서 그런 중년인의 모습을 지켜보는 두 사람이 있었다.
 14|
 15|“맞나? 저자가 바로 그……?”
 16|
 17|“바로 그 곽철융일세. 확실해.”
 18|
 19|“세상에, 내 살다 살다 전설의 도곤을 직접 보게 될 줄이야.”
 20|
 21|각각 뱁새눈과 염소수염이 인상적인 두 사내는 어디서나 볼 수 있는 그저 그런 도박꾼들이었다.
 22|
 23|다시 골패를 돌리는 곽철융을 모습을 바라보던 염소수염이 물었다.
 24|
 25|“그런데 꼴이 왜 저래?”
 26|
 27|그의 물음처럼 곽철융의 행색은 말이 아니었다.
 28|
 29|초췌한 안색과 손질이 되지 않은 수염. 때가 새카맣게 묻은 비단옷은 군데군데 찢어져 있었다.
 30|
 31|일평생 노름판을 전전하며 엄청난 부를 쌓았다는 그다.
 32|
 33|그러나 지금의 모습은 실패한 도박꾼, 그 이상도 이하도 아니었다.
 34|
 35|“무슨 일이라도 있었나?”
 36|
 37|“있었지. 그것도 아주 큰 일이.”
 38|
 39|뱁새눈이 고개를 끄덕였다. 뒤늦게 하남에 도착한 염소수염과 달리 그는 최근 곽철융에게 벌어진 일에 대해 잘 알고 있었다.
 40|
 41|“그게 뭔가? 애타게 하지 말고 좀 알려 주게.”
 42|
 43|“도박에서 졌거든.”
 44|
 45|“이 바닥에서 이기고 지는 거야 흔한 일 아닌가?”
 46|
 47|“흔한 일이지. 하지만 은자 천 냥짜리 판이라면 어떤가?”
 48|
 49|“헉! 은자 천 냥!”
 50|
 51|염소수염이 눈을 부릅떴다.
 52|
 53|그 정도면 평생 호의호식할 수 있는, 아니 삼 대가 떵떵거릴 수 있을 만큼 천문학적인 금액 아닌가.
 54|
 55|그는 그토록 큰 판을 보지 못했다는 아쉬움에 입맛을 다시며 물었다.
 56|
 57|“건국 이래 최고의 승부였겠군. 상대는 누구였나? 아귀? 아니면 짝귀?”
 58|
 59|“이 친구, 귀 어두운 거야 진작 알고 있었지만 요즘 소식에 영 깜깜하군. 아귀는 두어 달 전에 청성산 작두라는 놈한테 손목이 잘렸고, 짝귀는 잠적한 지 오래됐어.”
 60|
 61|“그럼 그 둘 말고 누가 천하의 곽철융을 이겨?”
 62|
 63|“산서잠룡.”
 64|
 65|“누구?”
 66|
 67|“태원진가의 진태경, 화왕의 제자지.”
 68|
 69|화왕은 십왕 중 일인이자 천하에 위명이 쟁쟁한 초절정 고수. 그런 자의 제자가 도곤과 노름을 할 일은 없다.
 70|
 71|잠시 머리를 굴리던 염소수염이 탄식처럼 외쳤다.
 72|
 73|“도도(賭賭)! 성라대연 도도를 했군.”
 74|
 75|“정답일세.”
 76|
 77|성라대연의 내기 도박은 천하 각지에서 벌어지는 도박 중 제일이라 하여 도도라 부른다.
 78|
 79|마침내 사태를 파악한 염소수염이 혀를 찼다.
 80|
 81|“쯧쯧. 곽철융이 멍청한 짓을 했군. 예선 배당률이 높긴 하지만 그만큼 위험하다는 것도 생각했어야지.”
 82|
 83|“그가 아무런 생각도 없이 걸었겠나. 나름대로 확신이 있었던 거겠지.”
 84|
 85|“누구한테 어떻게 걸었는데?”
 86|
 87|“철수신룡의 예선 수석.”
 88|
 89|“글쎄, 해상왕의 제자이니 강하긴 하겠지만 딱히 그 정도까지는 아닐 것 같은데.”
 90|
 91|뱁새눈이 고개를 저었다.
 92|
 93|“최근에 깨달음을 얻은 모양이야. 철수신룡의 파선권에 절벽의 십분지 일이 날아갔다는군.”
 94|
 95|“……그게 말이 되나?”
 96|
 97|무림의 고수들이 땅을 부수고 하늘을 가른다는 소문은 들었지만, 설마 이 정도일 줄이야.
 98|
 99|염소수염이 놀라움을 금치 못하던 그때, 귀를 의심케 하는 한마디가 더 이어졌다.
100|
101|“말이 안 될 건 뭔가? 바로 그 직후에 산서잠룡은 절벽을 무너트리기까지 했는데.”
102|
103|“……!”
104|
105|염소수염이 접시만 해진 눈으로 더듬더듬 물었다.
106|
107|“저, 절벽을 무너트렸다고?”
108|
109|“맞네. 목격자들의 증언에 따르면, 아주 와르르 무너졌다더군.”
110|
111|“…….”
112|
113|염소수염은 대답하지 않았다. 대신 불신 어린 눈빛으로 자신의 친우를 응시했다.
114|
115|“헛소문 아닌가?”
116|
117|“나를 포함한 다른 이들도 처음에는 헛소문이라고 치부했네. 피육으로 이루어진 사람이 맨손으로 절벽을 무너트린다는 게 말이 되는 일은 아니니까.”
118|
119|“내 말이.”
120|
121|“하지만 사실인 걸 어쩌겠나. 저기 있는 곽철융이 대표적인 산증인이지.”
122|
123|“곽철융이 왜…… 아, 은자 천 냥을 잃었겠군.”
124|
125|“오천 냥일세.”
126|
127|“뭐?”
128|
129|“반드시 이길 것 같았던 판에서 돈을 잃으면 어떨 것 같나?”
130|
131|“호, 혹시.”
132|
133|“곽철융이라고 별수 있나. 결국 도박에 미친 것은 매한가지인 것을.”
134|
135|뱁새눈은 딱하다는 눈빛으로 곽철융을 바라보았다.
136|
137|꾀죄죄한 몰골의 그는 멍한 얼굴로 자신의 패를 들여다보고 있었다.
138|
139|“사흘 전 그날, 철수신룡이 성라대연을 포기하고 장강으로 돌아가자 곽철융은 눈이 뒤집혀 버렸지.”
140|
141|“도도를 계속한 건가?”
142|
143|뱁새눈이 고개를 끄덕였다.
144|
145|“곽철융이 철수신룡 다음으로 선택한 것은 혼뢰각(倱雷脚) 종삼이었네. 그가 각법 심사에서 최고점을 달성하는 것에 걸었지.”
146|
147|“각법으로는 광서 땅에서 따라올 자가 없다는 그 절정 고수?”
148|
149|“응. 근데 이제는 따라올 사람이 꽤 많을 걸세. 한쪽 다리가 부러졌거든.”
150|
151|“설마 그것도 산서잠룡인가?”
152|
153|“슬슬 감이 잡히나? 맞네. 둘이 사소한 시비가 붙어서 깔끔하게 한 대씩 주고받고 끝내기로 했는데, 산서잠룡의 발차기 한 방에 정강이가 부러졌다더군.”
154|
155|“어, 어떻게?”
156|
157|“몰라. 툭 차니까 우두둑 부러졌대.”
158|
159|“…….”
160|
161|“심지어 혼뢰각이 선방을 쳤는데, 산서잠룡은 종아리 몇 번 긁고 끝났다던가. 그리고 그다음이 아마…….”
162|
163|그 후에도 뱁새눈의 입에서 계속해서 흘러나오는 산서잠룡의 행보는 경악 그 자체였다.
164|
165|천하의 후기지수 중 경공술이 가장 뛰어나다는 곤륜파의 곤륜운룡(崑崙雲龍)은 제자리에서 오 장을 도약했으나 진태경에게 얼굴을 밟힌 채 추락.
166|
167|개방의 후개(後丐)는 신법 심사 도중 진태경과의 차이를 도무지 좁히지 못하자 극대노. 분을 참지 못해 그의 뒷덜미를 잡았다가 말 그대로 개처럼 처맞았다고 했다.
168|
169|“다섯 번째 심사는 기관진식(機關陣式)이었지. 이번만큼은 모두가 제갈세가의 소가주가 수석을 차지할 거라 믿었지만…….”
170|
171|넋 나간 얼굴로 이야기를 듣고 있던 염소수염이 말을 잘랐다.
172|
173|“또 산서잠룡이겠지.”
174|
175|“바로 맞췄네.”
176|
177|“아무리 그래도 그렇지. 도대체 어떻게 된 놈이기에 기관진식에도 능통하단 말인가?”
178|
179|“아니. 그냥 무공에 능통해. 이 무식한 놈이 뭐가 뭔지 모르겠으니까 그냥 죄다 부수면서 통과했다는군.”
180|
181|“…….”
182|
183|“여하간 그렇게 산서잠룡이 이번 예선의 수석이 되었고, 매번 다른 곳에다 걸었던 곽철융은 개털이 된 거지. 지금까지 번 돈에, 은퇴 후 지낼 장원과 땅까지 담보로 잡아 고리대금을 끌어 썼다는데…… 쯧쯧.”
184|
185|뱁새눈은 안타까운 듯한 눈빛으로 곽철융을 바라봤다.
186|
187|한때 엄청난 부를 축적했던 전설적인 도곤의 앞에는 은자 몇 냥이 전부였다. 그리고 아마도 그것이 그의 전 재산일 터였다.
188|
189|“버는 것도 한 방. 날리는 것도 한 방이야. 안 그런가?”
190|
191|그제야 비로소 정신을 차린 염소수염이 바짝 마른 입술을 핥았다.
192|
193|“은자 오천 냥이라니. 어느 놈이 땄는지는 몰라도 대박이 났겠군.”
194|
195|“제대로 노났지. 오죽하면 금면공자(金面公子)라고 불리겠나.”
196|
197|“금면공자? 그놈이 산서잠룡한테 걸었나?”
198|
199|뱁새눈이 고개를 끄덕였다.
200|
201|“선견지명이 대단한 놈이야. 이번 도도에서 족히 은자 수만 냥은 땄을걸? 오죽하면 금으로 된 가면을 쓰고 다니겠나.”
202|
203|“허어어.”
204|
205|“아직 이립도 안 된 젊은 놈이라는데…… 이래서 될 놈은 된다는 거겠지.”
206|
207|“염병. 누구는 이 나이까지 제대로 된 집 한 채 없는데. 후우…….”
208|
209|두 사람이 한숨을 푹 내쉰 그때, 의자 끌리는 소리와 함께 한 사람이 자리에서 일어났다.
210|
211|비틀거리는 걸음으로 도박장을 빠져나가는 곽철융이 손에 쥔 것은 개평으로 받은 철전 몇 푼이 전부였다.
212|
213|
214|
215|* * *
216|
217|
218|
219|성라대연은 최소 보름에서 길면 한 달까지 이어지는 장기 레이스다.
220|
221|사흘간에 걸친 예선 심사가 끝나자 지원자들에게는 하루 동안의 자유 시간이 주어졌고, 그것은 내게도 해당하는 사안이었다.
222|
223|“어험. 어흐흠!”
224|
225|“막내야, 막내야아!”
226|
227|“조장님! 조장니이이임!”
228|
229|“……아, 제발.”
230|
231|그러지 마. 이렇게 사람 많은 곳에서 소리 지르지 마. 안 그래도 주위 시선들이 신경 쓰여 죽겠는데 더 쳐다보잖아.
232|
233|타다다다닥!
234|
235|나는 누구보다 빠른 걸음으로 일행에게 다가갔다. 기다렸다는 듯이 곰 같은 덩치의 진위경이 팔을 벌린 채 쇄도해 왔다.
236|
237|“막내야! 장한 내 아우야!”
238|
239|후웅! 덥석!
240|
241|곰 발바닥이 상반신을 옥죄는 것과 동시에, 혁무진이 내 손등을 잡고 볼을 비볐다.
242|
243|“오오, 조장님! 성라대연 수석! 태원진가의 자랑! 산서성의 등불! 우리 조장님! 나의 주군이시여!”
244|
245|“…….”
246|
247|진위경이라 그렇다 치고 혁무진 이 자식은 왜 이러는 걸까.
248|
249|나는 황당함을 애써 감추며 물었다.
250|
251|“너 돌았니?”
252|
253|“예. 미쳤습니다! 저는 조장님의 강함에 미쳐 버렸습니다!”
254|
255|“진짜 미친놈인가. 놔, 빨리 안 놔?”
256|
257|빡! 빡! 빡!
258|
259|빛살 같은 속도로 정수리에 삼 연타를 먹였음에도 혁무진은 요지부동이었다.
260|
261|고통에 눈물을 찔끔 흘리면서도 끝까지 손을 놓지 않는다.
262|
263|“감사합니다! 때려 주셔서 감사합니다!”
264|
265|“……너 혹시 그쪽이냐?”
266|
267|말로만 들었다. 맞으면서 쾌락을 느끼는 사람이 있다고.
268|
269|지금껏 내게 수도 없이 맞았는데도 왜 떠나지 않았는지 의문이었는데, 그쪽이라고 생각하니 등줄기를 타고 소름이 쭉 돋았다.
270|
271|“취향존중권!”
272|
273|퍽!
274|
275|정확하게 관자놀이를 얻어맞은 혁무진이 털썩 쓰러진다.
276|
277|동시에 녀석의 품 안에서 번쩍거리는 뭔가가 바닥에 툭 떨어졌다.
278|
279|“엥? 금가면?”
280|
281|이건 또 뭐야.
282|
283|그런 종류의 플레이를 할 때 사용하는 소품인가. 나는 심각한 얼굴로 가면을 품에 챙겼다.
284|
285|혁무진 이 위험한 새끼, 가면은 평생 압수다.
286|
287|‘어림도 없지.’
288|
289|각오를 다지던 그때, 잠시 잊고 있던 한 사람이 눈에 들어왔다.
290|
291|“어흠. 커흐흠!”
292|
293|“기관지 안 좋으세요?”
294|

The Fire King was one of the Ten Kings and a Supreme Peak master whose reputation resounded throughout the world. There was no reason for such a man’s disciple to gamble with a Dogon.

[P34]
After thinking for a moment, the goat-bearded man cried out.

[P35]
“Dodo![^1] He played Dodo at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

[P36]
“Correct.”

[P37]
The Star-Array Grand Banquet’s betting games were considered the greatest gambling matches anywhere under heaven, and were therefore called Dodo.

[P38]
At last, the goat-bearded man understood what had happened and clicked his tongue.

[P39]
“Tsk, tsk. Kwak Cheolyung did something stupid. The odds on the preliminaries may have been high, but he should have realized that meant the risk was high, too.”

[P40]
“Do you think he bet without thinking? He must have had his reasons for being confident.”

[P41]
“What did he bet on?”

[P42]
“The Iron-Water Divine Dragon taking first place in the preliminaries.”

[P43]
“I suppose he’s strong, being the Seafaring King’s disciple, but I don’t think he’s quite that good.”

[P44]
The narrow-eyed man shook his head.

[P45]
“He seems to have gained some insight recently. I heard the Iron-Water Divine Dragon blew away a tenth of a cliff with his Ship-Breaking Fist.”

[P46]
“…Is that even possible?”

[P47]
The goat-bearded man had heard tales of Murim masters shattering the earth and cleaving the sky, but he had never imagined they were capable of anything like that.

[P48]
While he was still reeling in astonishment, the narrow-eyed man said something even harder to believe.

[P49]
“What’s so impossible about it? Right afterward, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi brought down the entire cliff.”

[P50]
“…!”

[P51]
The goat-bearded man’s eyes grew as wide as plates.

[P52]
“H-He brought down a cliff?”

[P53]
“That’s right. According to the witnesses, the whole thing came crashing down.”

[P54]
“……”

[P55]
The goat-bearded man said nothing. He merely stared at his friend in disbelief.

[P56]
“Isn’t that just a wild rumor?”

[P57]
“Everyone else, myself included, dismissed it as one at first. A man of flesh and blood bringing down a cliff with his bare hands? It didn’t seem possible.”

[P58]
“Exactly.”

[P59]
“But what can we do when it’s true? Kwak Cheolyung sitting over there is living proof.”

[P60]
“Why would Kwak Cheolyung be proof…? Ah. He must have lost a thousand silver nyang.”

[P61]
“Five thousand.”

[P62]
“What?”

[P63]
“What do you think happens when someone loses money on a bet he was certain he’d win?”

[P64]
“C-Could it be…?”

[P65]
“Is Kwak Cheolyung any different from the rest of us? In the end, he’s just as addicted to gambling.”

[P66]
The narrow-eyed man looked at Kwak Cheolyung with pity.

[P67]
The disheveled man was staring blankly at the tiles in his hand.

[P68]
“Three days ago, when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon withdrew from the Star-Array Grand Banquet and returned to the Yangtze, Kwak Cheolyung completely lost his mind.”

[P69]
“Did he keep playing Dodo?”

[P70]
The narrow-eyed man nodded.

[P71]
“After the Iron-Water Divine Dragon, Kwak Cheolyung chose Jong Sam of the Hunroe Leg. He bet on him receiving the highest score in the leg-technique assessment.”

[P72]
“That Peak master said to have no equal in kicks throughout Guangxi?”

[P73]
“Yes. Though by now, he probably has plenty of equals. One of his legs is broken.”

[P74]
“Don’t tell me the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi did that, too.”

[P75]
“Starting to see the pattern? That’s right. The two of them got into a minor dispute and agreed to exchange one clean blow each, then call it even. But a single kick from the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi broke Jong Sam’s shin.”

[P76]
“H-How?”

[P77]
“I don’t know. They say he gave it a light kick, and the bone snapped with a crunch.”

[P78]
“……”

[P79]
“The Hunroe Leg even struck first, but the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi just scratched his calf a few times afterward, and that was it. And next was probably…”

[P80]
The stories that continued pouring from the narrow-eyed man’s mouth were nothing short of shocking.

[P81]
The Kunlun Sect’s Kunlun Cloud Dragon, said to possess the finest lightness technique among all the young prodigies under heaven, leaped five jang from a standing position—only to come crashing down with Jin Taekyung’s foot planted on his face.

[P82]
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar flew into a rage when he could not close the distance between himself and Jin Taekyung during the movement-technique assessment. Unable to contain his anger, he grabbed Taekyung by the back of the neck and was promptly beaten like a dog.

[P83]
“The fifth assessment was mechanisms and formations. This time, everyone was certain the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head would take first place, but…”

[P84]
The goat-bearded man, who had been listening with a vacant expression, cut him off.

[P85]
“It was the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi again, wasn’t it?”

[P86]
“Exactly.”

[P87]
“But seriously, how? What kind of freak is proficient in mechanisms and formations, too?”

[P88]
“He isn’t. He’s just proficient in martial arts. The ignorant bastard had no idea what anything was, so he smashed everything in his path and forced his way through.”

[P89]
“……”

[P90]
“Anyway, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi took first place in the preliminaries, and Kwak Cheolyung, who bet on someone different every time, was left penniless. I heard he lost everything he’d ever earned, then mortgaged the estate and land where he’d planned to retire so he could borrow from loan sharks… Tsk, tsk.”

[P91]
The narrow-eyed man gazed at Kwak Cheolyung with sympathy.

[P92]
Only a few silver nyang sat before the legendary Dogon who had once amassed a tremendous fortune. They were probably all he had left in the world.

[P93]
“Whether you make a fortune or lose one, it all happens in a single stroke. Isn’t that right?”

[P94]
Only then did the goat-bearded man come to his senses. He licked his parched lips.

[P95]
“Five thousand silver nyang. Whoever won that must have hit the jackpot.”

[P96]
“He certainly struck it rich. Why else would they call him the Gold-Faced Young Master?”

[P97]
“The Gold-Faced Young Master? Did he bet on the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”

[P98]
The narrow-eyed man nodded.

[P99]
“He has incredible foresight. He must have won tens of thousands of silver nyang from this Dodo alone. Why else would he go around wearing a mask made of gold?”

[P100]
“Good heavens.”

[P101]
“They say he hasn’t even turned thirty yet… I suppose some men are simply destined to succeed.”

[P102]
“Damn it. Some of us have reached this age without even owning a proper house. Hoo…”

[P103]
The two men let out deep sighs.

[P104]
Then a chair scraped across the floor as someone rose to his feet.

[P105]
Kwak Cheolyung staggered out of the gambling den. All he held were a few iron coins he had received as a consolation handout.

[P106]
* * *

[P107]
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a long race, lasting at least half a month and sometimes as long as a full month.

[P108]
After the three-day preliminary assessments ended, the applicants were given a day of free time.

[P109]
That included me.

[P110]
“Ahem. Ahehem!”

[P111]
“Youngest! Youngest!”

[P112]
“Captain! Captaiiin!”

[P113]
“…Oh, please.”

[P114]
*Don’t. Don’t shout in a place this crowded. I’m already dying from all the attention, and now you’re making even more people stare.*

[P115]
Tap-tap-tap-tap!

[P116]
I hurried toward my companions as quickly as I could.

[P117]
As though he had been waiting for me, Jin Wikyung’s bear-like bulk charged forward with both arms spread wide.

[P118]
“Youngest! My wonderful little brother!”

[P119]
Whoosh! Grab!

[P120]
The moment his bear paw locked around my upper body, Hyuk Mujin seized the back of my hand and rubbed his cheek against it.

[P121]
“Ohhh, Captain! Top scorer in the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries! The pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan! The beacon of Shanxi Province! Our Captain! My lord!”

[P122]
“……”

[P123]
*Wikyung is one thing, but what the hell is wrong with Hyuk Mujin?*

[P124]
Doing my best to hide my bewilderment, I asked, “Are you out of your mind?”

[P125]
“Yes. I’m insane! Your strength has driven me mad!”

[P126]
“Are you seriously crazy? Let go. Let go already!”

[P127]
Whack! Whack! Whack!

[P128]
Even after I struck the crown of his head three times at lightning speed, Hyuk Mujin refused to budge.

[P129]
Tears welled in his eyes from the pain, but he still would not release my hand.

[P130]
“Thank you! Thank you for hitting me!”

[P131]
“…Are you into that kind of thing?”

[P132]
I had only heard rumors about people who took pleasure in being hit.

[P133]
I had always wondered why he had never left despite the countless beatings I had given him. Now that I considered the possibility that he was one of those people, a chill ran down my spine.

[P134]
“Respect-Your-Preferences Fist!”

[P135]
Thump!

[P136]
The blow landed squarely on Hyuk Mujin’s temple, and he collapsed to the ground.

[P137]
At the same time, something bright and glittering slipped from inside his robes and landed on the floor.

[P138]
“Huh? A gold mask?”

[P139]
*What the hell is this?*

[P140]
*Is it a prop for that kind of play?*

[P141]
With a grave expression, I tucked the mask into my robes.

[P142]
*Hyuk Mujin, you dangerous bastard. This mask is confiscated for life.*

[P143]
*Not on my watch.*

[P144]
As I steeled my resolve, I noticed someone I had momentarily forgotten.

[P145]
“Ahem. Ahehem!”

[P146]
“Do you have bronchitis?”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring off at a distant mountain and repeatedly clearing his throat, flinched.

[P148]
“W-What nonsense are you spouting?”

[P149]
“You’ve been coughing this whole time.”

[P150]
“Ahem!”

[P151]
He kept looking away, clearly wanting to say something but pretending otherwise. The corners of my mouth rose on their own.

[P152]
“I did well, didn’t I?”

[P153]
“……”

[P154]
“Perfect scores in all five assessments. Unanimous first place overall. That pretty much says it all, doesn’t it?”

[P155]
“Ahem. Don’t get so pleased with yourself over something so trivial. Anyone could have done it, so stop making a fuss.”

[P156]
“I heard it was the first time in the history of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

[P157]
“These were merely the preliminaries. Have you forgotten what this old man told you? The world is vast, and there are many masters.”

[P158]
“I beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P159]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League. The Kunlun Cloud Dragon of the Kunlun Sect. And finally, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.

[P160]
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar was a master comparable to them, and the Hunroe Leg was a Peak master who had already made a brilliant name for himself throughout Guangxi.

[P161]
Their backgrounds and specialties were all different, but the five of them now had one thing in common.

[P162]
“I beat every last one of them.”

[P163]
“That…”

[P164]
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was at a loss for words. Then he shook his head.

[P165]
“Bah. Pathetic weaklings.”

[P166]
“I’m the strong one.”

[P167]
“There you go, acting cocky again.”

[P168]
“Could you just tell me I did well? I brought honor to you—Old Master, no, Master—and to the Fire Gate Clan.”

[P169]
“You still have a long way to go!”

[P170]
His words were stern, but the corners of his mouth were twitching.

[P171]
He was obviously struggling to hold back a smile.

[P172]
I would have known that even without the Sound Transmission Jin Wikyung sent me a moment later.

[P173]
—Don’t let it bother you too much. It seems he already went and bragged about you to the leadership to his heart’s content.

[P174]
“Ahem!”

[P175]
As if he had overheard us, Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat again at the perfect moment. Forcing a stern expression onto his face, he said, “Do not grow arrogant merely because you defeated a few nobodies. Compose your body and mind, and prepare for the main event. Understood?”

[P176]
He was right.

[P177]
Only the preliminaries had ended. The main event, where the true masters would reveal themselves, had not even begun.

[P178]
Among those who had passed through the sieve of the preliminaries, there were likely quite a few masters comparable to the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—or even stronger.

[P179]
I had already spotted several such people while watching the assessments.

[P180]
*The world really is vast. He was right about that.*

[P181]
Anyone who had concealed their true ability during the preliminaries was not only strong, but clever.

[P182]
I grinned and gave Jeok Cheongang a fist-and-palm salute.

[P183]
“I’ll keep that in mind, Master.”

[P184]
“That boy. Ha ha. Ahem!”

[P185]
An unmistakable smile appeared at the wrinkled corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.

[^1]: “Dodo” is the Star-Array Grand Banquet’s term for a gambling match; the name repeats the Chinese character for “gamble” (賭賭).

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 247

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃247화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|음습한 지하 도박장. 구석 자리에 앉아 골패를 만지작거리고 있던 중년인이 고개를 떨궜다.
  6|
  7|“……죽겠소.”
  8|
  9|그의 코에는 서역에서 들어온 안경이라는 물건이 걸쳐져 있었는데, 며칠 전만 해도 은자 수십 냥은 족히 나갈 물건이었지만 지금은 아니었다.
 10|
 11|사물을 몇 배나 키워서 보여 준다는 안경알이 가뭄이 든 논처럼 쩍쩍 금이 가 있었기 때문이다.
 12|
 13|먼발치에서 그런 중년인의 모습을 지켜보는 두 사람이 있었다.
 14|
 15|“맞나? 저자가 바로 그……?”
 16|
 17|“바로 그 곽철융일세. 확실해.”
 18|
 19|“세상에, 내 살다 살다 전설의 도곤을 직접 보게 될 줄이야.”
 20|
 21|각각 뱁새눈과 염소수염이 인상적인 두 사내는 어디서나 볼 수 있는 그저 그런 도박꾼들이었다.
 22|
 23|다시 골패를 돌리는 곽철융을 모습을 바라보던 염소수염이 물었다.
 24|
 25|“그런데 꼴이 왜 저래?”
 26|
 27|그의 물음처럼 곽철융의 행색은 말이 아니었다.
 28|
 29|초췌한 안색과 손질이 되지 않은 수염. 때가 새카맣게 묻은 비단옷은 군데군데 찢어져 있었다.
 30|
 31|일평생 노름판을 전전하며 엄청난 부를 쌓았다는 그다.
 32|
 33|그러나 지금의 모습은 실패한 도박꾼, 그 이상도 이하도 아니었다.
 34|
 35|“무슨 일이라도 있었나?”
 36|
 37|“있었지. 그것도 아주 큰 일이.”
 38|
 39|뱁새눈이 고개를 끄덕였다. 뒤늦게 하남에 도착한 염소수염과 달리 그는 최근 곽철융에게 벌어진 일에 대해 잘 알고 있었다.
 40|
 41|“그게 뭔가? 애타게 하지 말고 좀 알려 주게.”
 42|
 43|“도박에서 졌거든.”
 44|
 45|“이 바닥에서 이기고 지는 거야 흔한 일 아닌가?”
 46|
 47|“흔한 일이지. 하지만 은자 천 냥짜리 판이라면 어떤가?”
 48|
 49|“헉! 은자 천 냥!”
 50|
 51|염소수염이 눈을 부릅떴다.

The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar flew into a rage when he could not close the distance between himself and Jin Taekyung during the movement-technique assessment. Unable to contain his anger, he grabbed Taekyung by the back of the neck and was promptly beaten like a dog.

[P83]
“The fifth assessment was mechanisms and formations. This time, everyone was certain the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head would take first place, but…”

[P84]
The goat-bearded man, who had been listening with a vacant expression, cut him off.

[P85]
“It was the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi again, wasn’t it?”

[P86]
“Exactly.”

[P87]
“But seriously, how? What kind of freak is proficient in mechanisms and formations, too?”

[P88]
“He isn’t. He’s just proficient in martial arts. The ignorant bastard had no idea what anything was, so he smashed everything in his path and forced his way through.”

[P89]
“……”

[P90]
“Anyway, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi took first place in the preliminaries, and Kwak Cheolyung, who bet on someone different every time, was left penniless. I heard he lost everything he’d ever earned, then mortgaged the estate and land where he’d planned to retire so he could borrow from loan sharks… Tsk, tsk.”

[P91]
The narrow-eyed man gazed at Kwak Cheolyung with sympathy.

[P92]
Only a few silver nyang sat before the legendary Dogon who had once amassed a tremendous fortune. They were probably all he had left in the world.

[P93]
“Whether you make a fortune or lose one, it all happens in a single stroke. Isn’t that right?”

[P94]
Only then did the goat-bearded man come to his senses. He licked his parched lips.

[P95]
“Five thousand silver nyang. Whoever won that must have hit the jackpot.”

[P96]
“He certainly struck it rich. Why else would they call him the Gold-Faced Young Master?”

[P97]
“The Gold-Faced Young Master? Did he bet on the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”

[P98]
The narrow-eyed man nodded.

[P99]
“He has incredible foresight. He must have won tens of thousands of silver nyang from this Dodo alone. Why else would he go around wearing a mask made of gold?”

[P100]
“Good heavens.”

[P101]
“They say he hasn’t even turned thirty yet… I suppose some men are simply destined to succeed.”

[P102]
“Damn it. Some of us have reached this age without even owning a proper house. Hoo…”

[P103]
The two men let out deep sighs.

[P104]
Then a chair scraped across the floor as someone rose to his feet.

[P105]
Kwak Cheolyung staggered out of the gambling den. All he held were a few iron coins he had received as a consolation handout.

[P106]

[P107]
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a long race, lasting at least half a month and sometimes as long as a full month.

[P108]
After the three-day preliminary assessments ended, the applicants were given a day of free time.

[P109]
That included me.

[P110]
“Ahem. Ahehem!”

[P111]
“Youngest! Youngest!”

[P112]
“Captain! Captaiiin!”

[P113]
“…Oh, please.”

[P114]
*Don’t. Don’t shout in a place this crowded. I’m already dying from all the attention, and now you’re making even more people stare.*

[P115]
Tap-tap-tap-tap!

[P116]
I hurried toward my companions as quickly as I could.

[P117]
As though he had been waiting for me, Jin Wikyung’s bear-like bulk charged forward with both arms spread wide.

[P118]
“Youngest! My wonderful little brother!”

[P119]
Whoosh! Grab!

[P120]
The moment his bear paw locked around my upper body, Hyuk Mujin seized the back of my hand and rubbed his cheek against it.

[P121]
“Ohhh, Captain! Top scorer in the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries! The pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan! The beacon of Shanxi Province! Our Captain! My lord!”

[P122]
“……”

[P123]
*Wikyung is one thing, but what the hell is wrong with Hyuk Mujin?*

[P124]
Doing my best to hide my bewilderment, I asked, “Are you out of your mind?”

[P125]
“Yes. I’m insane! Your strength has driven me mad!”

[P126]
“Are you seriously crazy? Let go. Let go already!”

[P127]
Whack! Whack! Whack!

[P128]
Even after I struck the crown of his head three times at lightning speed, Hyuk Mujin refused to budge.

[P129]
Tears welled in his eyes from the pain, but he still would not release my hand.

[P130]
“Thank you! Thank you for hitting me!”

[P131]
“…Are you into that kind of thing?”

[P132]
I had only heard rumors about people who took pleasure in being hit.

[P133]
I had always wondered why he had never left despite the countless beatings I had given him. Now that I considered the possibility that he was one of those people, a chill ran down my spine.

[P134]
“Respect-Your-Preferences Fist!”

[P135]
Thump!

[P136]
The blow landed squarely on Hyuk Mujin’s temple, and he collapsed to the ground.

[P137]
At the same time, something bright and glittering slipped from inside his robes and landed on the floor.

[P138]
“Huh? A gold mask?”

[P139]
*What the hell is this?*

[P140]
*Is it a prop for that kind of play?*

[P141]
With a grave expression, I tucked the mask into my robes.

[P142]
*Hyuk Mujin, you dangerous bastard. This mask is confiscated for life.*

[P143]
*Not on my watch.*

[P144]
As I steeled my resolve, I noticed someone I had momentarily forgotten.

[P145]
“Ahem. Ahehem!”

[P146]
“Do you have bronchitis?”

[P147]
Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring off at a distant mountain and repeatedly clearing his throat, flinched.

[P148]
“W-What nonsense are you spouting?”

[P149]
“You’ve been coughing this whole time.”

[P150]
“Ahem!”

[P151]
He kept looking away, clearly wanting to say something but pretending otherwise. The corners of my mouth rose on their own.

[P152]
“I did well, didn’t I?”

[P153]
“……”

[P154]
“Perfect scores in all five assessments. Unanimous first place overall. That pretty much says it all, doesn’t it?”

[P155]
“Ahem. Don’t get so pleased with yourself over something so trivial. Anyone could have done it, so stop making a fuss.”

[P156]
“I heard it was the first time in the history of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

[P157]
“These were merely the preliminaries. Have you forgotten what this old man told you? The world is vast, and there are many masters.”

[P158]
“I beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”

[P159]
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League. The Kunlun Cloud Dragon of the Kunlun Sect. And finally, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.

[P160]
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar was a master comparable to them, and the Hunroe Leg was a Peak master who had already made a brilliant name for himself throughout Guangxi.

[P161]
Their backgrounds and specialties were all different, but the five of them now had one thing in common.

[P162]
“I beat every last one of them.”

[P163]
“That…”

[P164]
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was at a loss for words. Then he shook his head.

[P165]
“Bah. Pathetic weaklings.”

[P166]
“I’m the strong one.”

[P167]
“There you go, acting cocky again.”

[P168]
“Could you just tell me I did well? I brought honor to you—Old Master, no, Master—and to the Fire Gate Clan.”

[P169]
“You still have a long way to go!”

[P170]
His words were stern, but the corners of his mouth were twitching.

[P171]
He was obviously struggling to hold back a smile.

[P172]
I would have known that even without the Sound Transmission Jin Wikyung sent me a moment later.

[P173]
—Don’t let it bother you too much. It seems he already went and bragged about you to the leadership to his heart’s content.

[P174]
“Ahem!”

[P175]
As if he had overheard us, Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat again at the perfect moment. Forcing a stern expression onto his face, he said, “Do not grow arrogant merely because you defeated a few nobodies. Compose your body and mind, and prepare for the main event. Understood?”

[P176]
He was right.

[P177]
Only the preliminaries had ended. The main event, where the true masters would reveal themselves, had not even begun.

[P178]
Among those who had passed through the sieve of the preliminaries, there were likely quite a few masters comparable to the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—or even stronger.

[P179]
I had already spotted several such people while watching the assessments.

[P180]
*The world really is vast. He was right about that.*

[P181]
Anyone who had concealed their true ability during the preliminaries was not only strong, but clever.

[P182]
I grinned and gave Jeok Cheongang a fist-and-palm salute.

[P183]
“I’ll keep that in mind, Master.”

[P184]
“That boy. Ha ha. Ahem!”

[P185]
An unmistakable smile appeared at the wrinkled corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
